assistant.content:
Below is a set of discreet—but clearly visible—camera‐placement suggestions for an Airbnb property. They’re strictly limited to common and external areas (never in private spaces such as bedrooms or bathrooms), and include the key legal and comfort considerations you’ll need to stay compliant.

GENERAL RULES  
• Disclose every camera, in your listing and with on-site signage.  
• Do not record in areas where guests expect full privacy (bedrooms, bathrooms, changing areas).  
• Audio recording is illegal or highly restricted in many jurisdictions—omit microphones unless you’ve checked local wiretapping laws and clearly notified guests.  
• Comply with all state/country requirements on notification, signage, retention periods and data protection.

1. MAIN ENTRANCE (EXTERIOR)  
  – Location: Centered above the front door, mounted under the porch overhang.  
  – Equipment: Weatherproof dome or bullet camera, 120° wide-angle lens.  
  – Visibility: Visible to satisfy “no hidden cameras” rules, but tucked under eaves so it isn’t obtrusive.  
  – Coverage: Captures every arrival/departure.

2. BACKYARD / PATIO AREA  
  – Location: Under a pergola beam or soffit corner.  
  – Equipment: Recessed or low-profile dome with infrared LEDs.  
  – Visibility: Paint-matched to structure; guests can still see the lens.  
  – Coverage: Seating, grill and gate access.

3. DRIVEWAY & GARAGE ENTRANCE  
  – Location: Above garage door or on adjacent wall, angled to capture license plates.  
  – Equipment: Outdoor bullet with at least 1080p resolution and night-vision.  
  – Privacy tip: Angle carefully to avoid filming neighbors’ yards.

4. LIVING ROOM / COMMON SITTING AREA  
  – Location: High corner opposite the main sofa or TV, 8–12 ft off the floor.  
  – Equipment: Indoor dome with 90–120° lens, recessed-style housing.  
  – Visibility: Small LED indicator; paint-trim to blend in.

5. KITCHEN / DINING SPACE  
  – Location: Above the refrigerator, or inside a top-cabinet with a tinted glass door.  
  – Equipment: Wide dynamic-range dome; optional “camouflage” housing.  
  – Coverage: Entire prep and dining area, without being overly conspicuous.

6. HALLWAY / CORRIDOR (TO PRIVATE ROOMS)  
  – Location: Ceiling-mounted in the center of a short passage.  
  – Equipment: 360° fisheye or 90° dome—choose based on hallway width.  
  – Purpose: Monitors foot traffic in and out of guest sleeping areas without filming inside them.

7. STAIRWELL (MULTI-LEVEL UNITS)  
  – Location: At the top of the stairs, angled slightly downward.  
  – Equipment: Low-profile dome or puck camera.  
  – Coverage: Tracks movement between floors.

8. SIDE GATE / SECONDARY ENTRANCE  
  – Location: Mounted on a fence post or on the side wall of the house.  
  – Equipment: Camouflaged as a utility box (still clearly visible).  
  – Visibility: Place a small “Security Camera in Use” sign nearby.

TECHNICAL & INSTALLATION CONSIDERATIONS  
• Height & Angle: 8–15 ft high, 30–45° downward tilt to avoid blind spots.  
• Power & Connectivity: Power-over-Ethernet (PoE) for reliability; hide cables in conduit or inside walls.  
• Optics: 2–4K resolution, wide dynamic range, IR or color night vision.  
• Data Security: Encrypted storage, strong unique passwords, two-factor authentication.  
• Motion Zones & Privacy Masks: Limit recording to areas of interest; mask out windows or neighbor properties.

GUEST-COMFORT & TRANSPARENCY  
• Listing Disclosure: Detail each camera’s location in your Airbnb description.  
• On-Site Map: Provide guests a simple floorplan showing camera spots.  
• Signage: Post “Video Surveillance in Use” signs at all entrances (inside and out).  
• Retention Policy: Only keep footage for the minimum legal period, then securely delete it.

LEGAL & POLICY CHECKLIST  
• Confirm your state/country laws on video and audio surveillance.  
• Adhere to Airbnb’s security device policy (no cameras in private areas; full disclosure).  
• Post any required local signage on your property’s perimeter or entrances.  
• Include camera disclosure in your rental agreement or house rules.  

By following these placement and disclosure guidelines you’ll achieve broad coverage of all high-traffic and external areas, maintain full legal compliance, and keep your guests’ comfort and privacy front and center.
